releases.notes:
Two fixes to the update machinery itself.

An appliance watches itself after an update and undoes the update if it does not come back healthy.
The previous release taught it to stop objecting to a setting ASCIA chooses on purpose — and Home
Assistant then reported *that* as something to object to, so a perfectly good update could still be
undone. The check now ignores both, and only reacts to things that undoing the update could
actually fix.

Second, the appliance now checks that a downloaded update is intact before it writes anything. A
damaged download was caught, but only halfway through installing, and it left the spare copy of the
system unusable in the process. It is now refused up front with a clear reason, and nothing is
touched.

Nothing about how your home behaves changes.
